topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The boundary of my space, the air thick with the scents of territory, melds with the quiet intonations of another. A request to intertwine the earth, to plant roots that will sip from the soil I tread. The idea sifts through my senses, stirring the fibers of the ground beneath me. The thought of shared space, of leaves and fruits mingling with what has been mine, kindles a warmth. It is not fear, nor anger, but a soft hum of possibility. The world is vast, and within it, this small corner can hold more than one heart, more than one set of steps. The answer comes easily, a silent nod, a stance that whispers of room to grow, together.
